channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Transport Vice-Minister Inspects Astana-1 Station Renovation
item.description: Kazakhstan's Transport Vice-Minister Zhanibek Taijanov inspected the ongoing renovation of Astana-1 railway station. The project is part of a larger program to modernize 124 stations. Major structural work is complete, with interior finishing and utility installations underway. The minister urged contractors to maintain construction pace and quality.

item.title: Turkey: Uzbekistan Central to Future Central Asian Developments, Says Former Envoy
item.description: Former Turkish Ambassador Hulusi Kılıç stated that Uzbekistan is central to processes shaping Central Asia's future. He noted increased regional leader meetings and joint problem-solving. Kılıç highlighted Uzbekistan's influential role in regional diplomacy, citing President Mirziyoyev's recent visit to Turkmenistan and his proposal for integrated regional cooperation beyond trade.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Islamic Civilization Center Showcases Heritage at UNESCO
item.description: The Center for Islamic Civilization presented Uzbekistan's heritage at UNESCO headquarters in Paris. This international conference, attended by over 300 scholars and diplomats, highlighted Central Asia's scientific and spiritual contributions to global civilization. The event aligns with President Mirziyoyev's initiative to promote the region's rich intellectual legacy.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Evolving Role in the Commonwealth of Independent States After 35 Years
item.description: After 35 years, the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) faces a changing global economy and logistics. For Uzbekistan, this means a shift from nation-building to concrete results like increased trade, joint ventures, and improved transport infrastructure. The country is increasingly asserting itself as an independent player in international relations within the CIS framework.

item.title: UN Report Highlights Devastating Impact of Afghanistan's Crisis on Children
item.description: A UN report details Afghanistan's complex crisis, including insecurity, poverty, and rights restrictions, which severely impact children. The report notes 1,415 child casualties in three years and an 81% rise in child recruitment by the Taliban, with some recruits as young as 12. Widespread rights violations against children are ongoing.

item.title: Fighter Jets Patrol Kunar Province Amid Reports of Drones Over Kabul
item.description: Local sources report fighter jets patrolling Kunar province, with Taliban fighters reportedly firing at them. Unidentified drones are also observed over Kabul. Clashes between Taliban and Pakistani forces in Paktia province have concluded, with no details on casualties or drone objectives provided.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Vice Minister of Transport Inspects Astana Old Station Reconstruction
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice Minister of Transport, Zhanibek Taijanov, inspected the reconstruction of the old railway station in Astana. Workers are currently focused on interior and exterior finishing, installing engineering systems, and constructing a passenger platform and concourse. The minister urged contractors to maintain construction pace and quality.

item.title: Clashes Reported Between Taliban and Pakistani Forces in Afghanistan's Paktia Province
item.description: Local sources report clashes between Taliban fighters and Pakistani forces in the Dand Patan and Aryob Zazi districts of Paktia province, Afghanistan. Heavy weapons were reportedly used by both sides. Some residents have fled their homes due to the fighting, which also saw Pakistani forces targeting several villages in Aryob Zazi district. Information on casualties is not yet available.

item.title: Taliban Forcibly Evict Residents from Homes in Nangarhar Despite Legal Documents
item.description: Taliban fighters raided the Angor Bagh area of Jalalabad city, forcibly evicting residents from at least 40 homes. Residents with legal ownership documents, some living there for decades, were ordered to vacate. The Taliban disregarded the documents, claiming the land belongs to a nomad close to a Taliban official. Hundreds are now displaced.

item.title: Trump Suggests Ukraine Needs New President Capable of Making Deals
item.description: US President Donald Trump stated that Ukraine needs to find a new leader capable of making agreements. He criticized President Zelenskyy for not finalizing deals and suggested it's time for Ukraine to elect a new president. Trump also mentioned advising Zelenskyy on striking Russian oil facilities, deeming it a global issue.

item.title: Clashes Between Taliban Forces and Pakistan in Border Areas of Paktia Province
item.description: Clashes have reportedly occurred between Taliban forces and Pakistani security forces in the border areas of Paktia Province. Details regarding the cause and extent of the clashes remain scarce, with both sides yet to issue official statements. The incident highlights ongoing tensions along the Durand Line.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 7,500 Violations Found in Business Inspections Over Nine Months
item.description: In Uzbekistan, 7,500 violations were identified during inspections of business entities in the first nine months of the year. Of these, 938 were illegal inspections, and 6,560 involved violations of inspection procedures.

item.title: Houthi Attack on Riyadh International Airport Leaves Several Injured
item.description: An attack by Houthi forces on Riyadh International Airport has resulted in multiple injuries. The extent of the damage to the airport facilities and the number of casualties are still being assessed.

item.title: UN Human Rights Chief Calls U.S. Sanctions Against ICC 'Unacceptable'
item.description: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk has deemed U.S. sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC) as "unacceptable." He urged states party to the Rome Statute to protect the court's independence and ensure accountability.

item.title: CIS Summit in Turkmenistan Focuses on Trust, Cooperation, and Development
item.description: The CIS Council of Heads of State met in Turkmenistan, addressing current global political and economic shifts. Uzbekistan's President emphasized comprehensive cooperation, including industrial ties, security, and improving citizens' quality of life. The meeting aimed to foster dialogue and find solutions for shared interests.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Proceeds with Major International Forums Despite Airport Attacks
item.description: Saudi Arabia will proceed with major international business events in Riyadh as scheduled, despite recent attacks on its airports that caused casualties. The 25th WPC Energy Congress and the Future Investment Initiative are confirmed to proceed, with enhanced security measures for participants. Attacks on airports in Riyadh and Abha between October 6-10 resulted in fatalities and injuries.

item.title: UN Women Expresses Concern Over Taliban Detentions and Threats Against Women and Girls
item.description: UN Women in Afghanistan has voiced serious concern regarding the detention, arrest, and threats against women and girls by the Taliban. Reports indicate detentions for non-compliance with dress codes, such as not wearing a chador or appearing without a male guardian.

item.title: West Kazakhstan Department Head Fined for Illegally Closing Cafeteria
item.description: The head of a district sanitary-epidemiological department in West Kazakhstan was fined 432,500 tenge for illegally ordering the closure of a cafeteria. The official violated the Entrepreneurship Code by not notifying the prosecutor's office. The fine was fully collected, and authorities reminded the public that such violations carry administrative liability.

item.title: US Urged Israel to Strike Iran Alone Before Midterms, Media Reports
item.description: US media reports suggest Washington encouraged Israel to strike Iran independently before the midterm elections, wanting Tel Aviv to assume all political risks. However, reports indicate the US backed down from this demand after negotiations. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Teenager Sentenced to Five Years for Drug Trafficking After Believing Online Ad
item.description: A teenager in Shymkent has been sentenced to five years in prison for selling psychotropic substances. He was lured by social media advertisements promising easy earnings. The prosecution warned youth against trusting dubious online offers and emphasized the legal consequences of drug trafficking.

item.title: Constitutional Court Chairperson Participates in Venice Commission Plenary Session
item.description: The Chairperson of Kazakhstan's Constitutional Court, Elvira Azimova, attended the 148th plenary session of the European Commission for Democracy through Law (Venice Commission) in Venice. The session reviewed legal and institutional issues of several countries, focusing on constitutional changes, judicial independence, and human rights.

item.title: Chinese Scientists Establish Satellite Communication Link Between Arctic and Antarctic
item.description: Chinese scientists have successfully established a satellite communication link between the Arctic and Antarctic using the Guowang satellite system. The connection was made from ships in the Arctic to China's "Qinling" station in Antarctica, with data transmission speeds reaching 30 Mbps and latency under one second.

item.title: Energy and Water Minister Travels to Saudi Arabia for World Energy Forum
item.description: Afghanistan's Minister of Energy and Water, Mohammad Younus Akhundzada, has traveled to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, to attend the 17th World Energy Forum. The forum will bring together ministerial-level representatives from approximately 100 countries to discuss energy cooperation, opportunities, and the exchange of experiences.

item.title: Afghan Educator Donates $2.5 Million to Oxford for Afghan Women's Scholarships
item.description: Shabana Basij-Rasikh, founder of the School of Leadership, Afghanistan, has donated $2.5 million to establish a permanent scholarship at the University of Oxford for Afghan women. The scholarship will cover full tuition, living expenses, and include leadership training, aiming to provide educational access for women facing educational barriers.

item.title: Astana Resident Scams Five Individuals Under Guise of Marketplace Investments
item.description: A resident of Astana has been sentenced to six years in prison for defrauding five people. She offered online marketplace training, then convinced victims to invest money for goods, promising returns. The funds were misused, causing a total loss of 15.6 million tenge.

item.title: Flydubai Co-Pilot Planned 9/11-Style Attack on Tel Aviv, Prosecutors Say
item.description: A Flydubai co-pilot, identified as Hammam Al-Hammami from Oman, confessed to planning a suicide attack inspired by 9/11. He intended to crash a Boeing 737 Max into Ben Gurion Airport. The suspect had made reconnaissance flights and passed security checks before the attempted hijacking.

item.title: Kazakhstan Awarded Hosting Rights for 2027 World Judo Championships
item.description: Kazakhstan has been awarded the hosting rights for the 2027 World Judo Championships, with the event to be held in Astana. The flag handover ceremony took place in Baku during the current championships. This event is a significant qualifier for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

item.title: UN Report Details Devastating Consequences for Children in Afghanistan Due to Insecurity and Restrictions
item.description: A UN report by Secretary-General António Guterres highlights the devastating impact of insecurity, poverty, displacement, and explosive ordnance on children in Afghanistan. Increased border clashes with Pakistan have further affected them. Between 2023-2025, 4,582 grave violations against children were verified, with 1,415 killed or injured, 80% by explosive ordnance. The Taliban were attributed the largest number of violations.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Social Health Insurance Fund Saves 23.4 Billion Tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Finance reports that transferring the Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF) under its purview has prevented financial losses and restructured the system. An AI-based anti-fraud system helped save 23.4 billion tenge, with efforts underway to recover over 7.9 billion tenge in illegally paid funds. Savings are directed to healthcare financing.

item.title: Kyrgyz Journalist Honored with International Award for Opposition Reporting
item.description: An opposition journalist from Kyrgyzstan has been awarded an international prize for their work. The recognition highlights the journalist's contributions to independent reporting and their role in shedding light on critical issues within the country.

item.title: Kazakhstan Citizen Recovers Lost $10,000 in Tashkent Metro Thanks to Face ID Technology
item.description: A citizen of Kazakhstan accidentally dropped $10,000 (4.5 million tenge) in the Tashkent metro but was unaware of the loss until reaching the car market. A fellow passenger found the money and handed it to metro security. Uzbekistan's Interior Ministry used Face ID technology to identify and return the full amount to the owner.

item.title: Investigative Journalist Bolot Temirov Receives International 'The Albies' Award in London
item.description: Investigative journalist Bolot Temirov, whose materials were declared 'extremist' in Kyrgyzstan, has received the international 'The Albies' award from the 'For Justice' foundation. The award ceremony took place in London. The award recognizes the international recognition of Temirov's projects, Temirov Live and 'Ait, Ait Dese'.

item.title: Kazakhstan Prevents 23.4 Billion Tenge Losses After Social Health Fund Transfer to Finance Ministry
item.description: Kazakhstan has prevented financial losses of 23.4 billion tenge following the transfer of the Social Health Insurance Fund to the Ministry of Finance. The ministry reported that channels of funding leakage were identified and closed, with over 7.9 billion tenge illegally paid to providers being recovered through criminal cases. These recovered funds are being directed towards medical care payments.

item.title: Book on Islam Karimov's Main Opponent Presented in Istanbul and Samarkand
item.description: A two-volume biographical book, "The Man Who Woke Up Early," about Uzbek poet, dissident, and politician Muhammad Salih, the founder of the "Erk" opposition party, was presented in Istanbul. The book, authored by Karimberdi Turamurod, covers Salih's life in Uzbekistan until 1993 and his life in exile from then until the present. A presentation also took place in Samarkand.

item.title: US State Department Places Afghanistan in Tier 3 of Human Trafficking Report
item.description: The US Department of State has classified Afghanistan as Tier 3 in its 2026 Trafficking in Persons Report. This designation is due to concerns regarding forced labor, child exploitation, and insufficient protection for trafficking victims. The report indicates Afghanistan has not met minimum standards for combating human trafficking and has not made significant efforts to improve the situation.

item.title: Central Asian Summit Advances Regional Cooperation and International Standing
item.description: The consultative summit in Avaza marks a new phase of regional cooperation, strengthening Central Asia's international position. Key goals include deepening collaboration in trade, transport, energy, and technology. Uzbekistan proposed an international conference in Tashkent to foster dialogue on peace and connectivity, emphasizing increased trade and joint production.

item.title: Head of Kazakhstan's Constitutional Court Attends Venice Commission Meeting
item.description: The head of Kazakhstan's Constitutional Court, Elvira Azimova, participated in the 148th plenary session of the Venice Commission in Venice, Italy. Representatives from 47 countries discussed legislative reforms, judicial independence, and citizen rights. The session focused on legal expertise for eight countries, including Georgia, Poland, and Ukraine.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans Six-Month Ban on White Sugar Imports
item.description: Kyrgyzstan intends to prohibit the import of white sugar for a period of six months. This measure aims to regulate the domestic sugar market. The specific reasons and details of the ban are expected to be announced soon.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Canada Strengthen Cooperation in Geology and Resource Exploration
item.description: Uzbekistan and Canada are enhancing collaboration in geology, focusing on advanced technologies for seismic data processing and subsurface visualization. A meeting between Uzbekistan's Ministry of Mining and Geology and Canada's Thrust Belt Imaging (TBI) discussed potential partnerships in geophysics, exploration, and energy sectors.

item.title: OSCE Media Forum on Information Accuracy and Trust in Media Held in Bishkek
item.description: An OSCE media forum on information accuracy and trust in media for Central Asia took place in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. Organized by the OSCE Representative on Freedom of the Media, the event focused on strengthening cooperation and dialogue regarding media freedom, journalistic ethics, and ensuring information accuracy to build societal trust.
